title: Refactor dict-based records to Python dataclasses
description: Brownfield Python refactor: replace dict-based Point and Rectangle records with @dataclass equivalents. The existing helper functions must continue to work with the new dataclass instances.

injections.content:
from src.geometry import make_point, make_rect, distance, rect_area, rect_contains


def test_distance():
    p1 = make_point(0, 0)
    p2 = make_point(3, 4)
    assert distance(p1, p2) == 5.0


def test_rect_area():
    r = make_rect(0, 0, 5, 3)
    assert rect_area(r) == 15


def test_rect_contains():
    r = make_rect(0, 0, 10, 10)
    assert rect_contains(r, make_point(5, 5))
    assert not rect_contains(r, make_point(15, 5))

task_spec.prompt:
Refactor src/geometry.py to use dataclasses instead of dicts.

from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Point:
    x: float
    y: float

@dataclass
class Rect:
    x: float
    y: float
    width: float
    height: float

# Update factory functions to return dataclass instances:
def make_point(x, y) -> Point: return Point(x, y)
def make_rect(x, y, w, h) -> Rect: return Rect(x, y, w, h)

# Update helpers to use attribute access instead of dict keys:
def distance(p1: Point, p2: Point) -> float: use p1.x, p1.y etc.
def rect_area(r: Rect) -> float: use r.width, r.height
def rect_contains(r: Rect, p: Point) -> bool: use attribute access

All 5 tests in the solution test file must pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: Point and Rect are @dataclass types (not dicts)
make_point and make_rect return dataclass instances
distance, rect_area, rect_contains use attribute access
All 5 tests pass including new dataclass-specific tests

uv run python -c "from src.geometry import Point, Rect, make_point, make_rect" passes

Final pass: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
